user: Hi, I'm a freelance graphic designer and I opted for the 8% income tax rate.
response:
As a freelance graphic designer under the 8% income tax rate, your tax will be based on your gross sales or receipts, and you cannot deduct business expenses. If your income comes purely from your freelance work, you can reduce your taxable amount by PHP 250,000 before applying the 8% rate. However, if you have mixed income (from both freelance work and other sources), this reduction does not apply to your business income [S2, S3]. 

If you need help calculating your tax or have questions about your gross receipts, please provide that information.

BIR Form 2307 is the Certificate of Creditable Tax Withheld at Source. It is issued by a withholding agent to a taxpayer to certify the amount of tax withheld from income payments made to the taxpayer. This form serves as proof of tax payments that can be credited against the taxpayer's income tax liability when filing their tax returns [S3].

user: Can I deduct the cost of my new laptop?
response: Under the 8% income tax rate, you cannot deduct business expenses, including the cost of your new laptop. The 8% tax is based solely on your gross sales or receipts without any deductions for expenses [S1, S2].

user: If I choose the 8% rate for my freelance income, can I subtract the 250,000 first?
response: No, if you choose the 8% rate for your freelance income as a mixed-income earner, you cannot subtract the PHP 250,000. This amount is only applicable to individuals earning income purely from self-employment or practice of profession. Since you have both compensation income and freelance income, the PHP 250,000 reduction does not apply to your freelance income under the 8% rate [S1, S4].
